title: Maintenance or discontinuation of antidepressants in primary care
authors: Lewis G, Marston L, Duffy L, Freemantle N, Gilbody S, Hunter R, et al.
population: Adults aged 18 to 74 years in 150 UK general practices with at least two previous depressive episodes or at least 2 years of antidepressant use, taking citalopram 20 mg, sertraline 100 mg, fluoxetine 20 mg or mirtazapine 30 mg daily for at least 9 months, who had recovered and felt well enough to consider stopping
funder: Supported by the National Institute for Health Research (HTA Program 13/115/48). The trial was sponsored by University College London and funded by the National Institute for Health Research, with no commercial involvement.
authorConflicts: Disclosure forms are available with the full text at NEJM.org; they are not itemised in the article text that was read.
result: Double-blind; 238 assigned to maintenance and 240 to discontinuation, of whom 41 and 37 took sertraline. In the discontinuation group, citalopram, sertraline or mirtazapine was given at half dose for 1 month, then half dose on alternate days with placebo for 1 month, then placebo; fluoxetine 20 mg on alternate days for 1 month, then placebo. Relapse by 52 weeks in 92 of 238 (39%) with maintenance and 135 of 240 (56%) with discontinuation (hazard ratio 2.06, 95% CI 1.56 to 2.70). At 12 weeks, new or worsened withdrawal symptoms on the modified DESS 1.3 against 3.1 (difference 1.9, 95% CI 1.5 to 2.3). Serious adverse events 9 (4%) against 8 (3%); no deaths or suicide attempts.
